Key Message 1...Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms, some
severe, are expected into tonight.

Cyclonic S'erly to SW'erly flow aloft and embedded shortwave
troughs impact our region through tonight as a deepening 
mid/upper-level low wobbles SSE'ward from northern ON to the 
northern Great Lakes. At the surface, a consolidating and 
deepening low should wobble E'ward from the northern Great Lakes
toward southeastern ON amidst mid/upper-level divergence and 
MSLP falls downstream of the low aloft. This low track should 
allow a warm front to continue drifting NE'ward through the 
Finger Lakes and the Eastern Lake Ontario Region through this 
evening and usher-in a somewhat warmer and moister air mass at the 
surface and aloft, while a cold front will continue sweeping E'ward 
from Lower MI and should reach far-Western NY by daybreak Sunday. 
Intervals of sunshine and low-level WAA ahead of and behind the 
surface warm front will allow highs to reach mainly the mid 70's to 
lower 80's late this afternoon. Lows tonight should reach the mid 
50's to mid 60's around daybreak Sunday.

Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms are expected,
especially late this afternoon through tonight as weak to
moderate CAPE, including elevated CAPE is released by the
following: moist isentropic ascent ahead of shortwave trough 
axes, low-level convergence/moist ascent along the cold front, 
and downshear gust fronts interacting favorably with ambient 
low-level vertical wind shear in the warm sector. Note: the
warm front passage will likely continue to be accompanied by
dry weather as pockets of dry air at the surface and especially
aloft precede the surface warm front. Deep-layer bulk shear is 
expected to remain moderate and diurnal convective mixing of the
boundary layer is expected to yield steep low-level lapse rates
and moderate DCAPE through this early evening, west of roughly 
the Genesee Valley. Thus, severe thunderstorms capable of 
producing damaging straight-line wind gusts are a concern in and
especially west of the Genesee Valley. Steepening mid-level 
lapse rates associated with mid/upper-level cooling associated 
with the deepening low/trough aloft and resulting increase in 
MUCAPE in the hail growth zone may allow a severe storm or two 
to produce damaging hail the size of quarters. The severe storm 
threat should end by late evening, following the onset of 
boundary layer stabilization via nocturnal cooling. Note: lake- 
effect rain showers and thunderstorms are possible east and 
especially southeast of Lake Erie toward and especially by 
daybreak, as 850 mb temperatures cool to near 10C over the ~24C 
lake amidst rich (i.e abundant/deep) synoptic-scale low-level 
moisture, sizable lake-induced CAPE/lake-induced EL's as high 
as 15kft to 25kft above lake level develop, and W'erly mean low-
level flow veers quickly to NW'erly behind the cold front.

Key Message 2...Unsettled weather continues Sunday through Tuesday. 
Monday is expected to be the coolest day of the upcoming week.

Cyclonic flow aloft, mainly SW'erly on Sunday, should become
W'erly to NW'erly Sunday night through Tuesday as the
aforementioned mid/upper-level low wobbles E'ward from the
northern Great Lakes toward southern QC through Monday and then
NE'ward toward the Gulf of St. Lawrence on Tuesday. At the
surface, the aforementioned low will weaken gradually as it
wobbles NE'ward toward the Gulf of St. Lawrence and becomes 
vertically-stacked with the low aloft. The cold front should
sweep E'ward through the rest of our CWA by early evening.
Behind the front, a lake-aggregate surface trough should linger
over/near the eastern Great Lakes through Monday before a
surface ridge begins to build from the western Great Lakes by
Tuesday. This weather pattern evolution at the surface and aloft
will allow a cooler air mass to overspread our region behind the
cold front and then linger through Tuesday. Daytime highs 
should reach mainly the mid 60's to mid 70's on Sunday. The 
coolest highs are expected in the higher terrain of Western NY.
Daytime highs should reach only the 60's to lower 70's on
Monday, when the core of the cooler air mass is expected to
reside over our region. Slightly warmer highs, mainly in the mid
60's to mid 70's, are expected on Tuesday. Overnight lows should
reach mainly the upper 40's to mid 50's Sunday night and Monday
night. 

Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms are expected
along and ahead of Sunday's cold front. A few of these storms
may become severe roughly along and east of the Genesee Valley,
where peeks of sunshine and daytime warming may yield weak to
moderate boundary layer CAPE, steep low-level lapse rates, and 
moderate DCAPE amidst moderate deep-layer bulk shear in the warm
sector. Behind the cold front, periods of lake-effect rain 
showers and thunderstorms are expected primarily east and
